name: Queen's Gambit
blurb: White offers the c-pawn on move two to pull Black's d-pawn away from the centre. A solid, ambitious choice that this course covers against the Declined, Accepted, Slav and Semi-Slav.

ideas.d4: Takes a central square. The queen already guards d4, so the pawn is supported from move one.
ideas.d4 d5 c4: The Queen's Gambit. The c-pawn attacks d5 and tries to pull it away from the centre. If Black takes, White can usually win the pawn back.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3: Adds another attacker to d5 and develops toward the centre.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5: Pins the f6 knight to the queen. That knight defends d5, so the pin adds pressure there.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3: Opens a path for the f1 bishop and supports d4. The bishop can now go to d3, or take on c4 if Black captures there.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 N: The rook goes to the c-file, which tends to open once pawns are exchanged on d5 or c4.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3: Against the Accepted, White develops first. The knight stops ...e5, and the c4 pawn can be won back later.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3: Opens the f1 bishop's diagonal, so the bishop now attacks the c4 pawn.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3: Against the Slav, White develops the knight and keeps an eye on e5.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4: Stops ...b5, which would let Black hold on to the extra pawn. White will win c4 back later.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Bg5: Pins the knight against the queen, the same idea as against the Queen's Gambit Declined.
